newsitem.title: GERMANY: Partial Target access for all EU central banks - BdB.
newsitem.headline: Partial Target access for all EU central banks - BdB.

text.p: All European Union central banks should have technical access to the Target payment system, not only those of countries which have launched the single European currency, Germany's main banking association said on Monday.

The BdB group, which represents Germany's biggest commercial banks, said in a statement that access to Target could prepare countries who had not yet launched the Euro for their eventual participation in the system.
However the BdB noted that countries who had not joined the monetary union should not be able to create Euros by accessing intraday or overnight loans denominated in the future single currency.
"Otherwise the danger would arise that EMU participants could be at a competitive disadvantage," the BdB said.
Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer earlier this month also said European central banks of so-called "not-in" states should not gain unlimited access to Target.

The Bank of England has objected in strong terms to plans to limit its access to the planned wholesale payments system for the Euro, saying that restrictions placed on its access will disadvantage London as a financial centre.
